instrumentation: Isolated projects, system Chrome headless and real Playwright pointer/wheel input. Canvas bounds/computed-style wrappers add equal microtiming overhead. Latency ends at the first requestAnimationFrame observation of the exact DOM camera or object pose; it excludes compositor presentation delay. Inputs are counted as matched, superseded by a later committed pose, or pending, and final input plus persisted/reloaded state are asserted. CDP durations cover gesture plus 150ms settling; persistence polling is excluded. Fixture assets are synthetic and fixture media. These figures describe the measured scenes and input cadence.
notes: Independent review found that .board-object.first() addressed different grid positions across rounds because batch-created object IDs were random. These rounds are exploratory; their percentages do not establish a fixed-fixture comparison. The corrected harness uses sequential creation, fixed IDs, explicit drag target perf-object-00, and asserted fixture geometry.
The final comparison uses baseline-r2/r3 and candidate-r1/r2 with the identical updated harness. Per-round p95 values are retained; their mean is used only for reporting paired variation.

baseline-r1 is retained as exploratory evidence. It lacked complete input accounting, cancellation/persistence/reload assertions, activity media, and the same-path warm-up. Its latency ended at the RAF timestamp, whereas the final harness uses the actual observation clock. It is excluded from the final comparison.
The initial point fixture omitted captureState and the service rejected zero dimensions. The corrected fixture supplies the normal incomplete captureState.

Earlier hook fixture runs timed out or found identical geometry after obstacle height/width changes, because the action bar already occupied the upper clear space. The final resize case moves the obstacle top edge and changes its dimensions to exercise a required placement change.
Real pointer/wheel inputs drive measured gestures. Pointer cancellation separately uses a real drag followed by a synthetic pointercancel lifecycle event.

Playwright input pacing and host scheduling affect total gesture elapsed time. Script/layout duration, DOM response, observer counts, and full input/persistence checks are reported; compositor presentation latency is outside the measurement.
